question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Dolors Montserrat (PPE) Subject:

Since 2017, the European Union has imposed restrictive measures on Venezuela, which include individual sanctions, such as bans on entering the EU and asset freezes, against various high-ranking officials, including Delcy Rodríguez, for being responsible for human rights violations and for undermining democracy and the rule of law. According to recent reports, the Spanish Government has confirmed the invitation of Rodríguez, currently the acting President of Venezuela, to the Ibero-American Summit that will be held in Madrid in November 2026, despite the fact that she remains on the EU sanctions list. In view of the above: 1.

Do the Commission and the Vice-President / High Representative consider the invitation and possible presence in the EU of a person subject to an entry ban to be compatible with EU law and with the Council Decision concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in Venezuela?
Has the Commission been informed of any request by Spain for an exemption or derogation, and what would be the consequences of the Common Position being violated?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2026) EU sanctions on Venezuela provide for exemptions and derogations from the restrictions on admission established under this regime. In particular, Article 6 of Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074 provides for such an exemption when a Member State is bound by an obligation of international law, namely (a) as a host country to an international intergovernmental organisation; (b) as a host country to an international conference convened by, or under the auspices of, the UN; (c) under a multilateral agreement conferring privileges and immunities; or (d) under the 1929 Treaty of Conciliation concluded by the Holy See and Italy1. The Council shall be duly informed when a Member State grants such an exemption2. That Article also allows Member States to grant exemptions from the the restrictions on admission where travel of the listed person is justified on the grounds of urgent humanitarian need, or on grounds of attending intergovernmental meetings and meetings promoted by the Union, or hosted by a Member State holding the chairmanship in office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, where a political dialogue is conducted that directly promotes democracy, human rights and the rule of law in Venezuela3. Member States wishing to grant such exemptions have an obligation to notify the Council in writing and respect the procedure set out by that same Article4.

2017/2074 of 13 November 2017 concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in Venezuela, OJ L 295, 14.11.2017, p. 60. 2 Article 6, paragraph 5, of Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074. 3 Article 6, paragraph 6, of Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074. 4 Article 6, paragraph 7, of Council Decision (CFSP) 2017/2074.
